content:
Maya (Sales): Quick sync — AcmeHealth POC kickoff. They need private connectivity for a Redwood Private deployment. Constraints: no public egress except to S3 for logs, want scoped non-prod API keys, and they'd like to test both Hosted API via a private endpoint and a Dedicated pool later. Can we spell out a minimal network + routing checklist and next steps? cc @Raj @Sarah @Emma

Raj (Solutions): Quick clarifying q's: do they prefer Interface endpoints (PrivateLink) or VPC peering/TGW? For multi-account setups we usually recommend PrivateLink (interface endpoints into their VPC hitting our NLB). Peering works but brings routing complexity (no transitive routes unless TGW).

Sarah (NetEng): PrivateLink notes: customer creates Interface ENIs in each AZ/subnet they want traffic from. Recommend 1 subnet per AZ with spare IPs (we suggest /24 subnets to avoid ENI exhaustion for POCs). Enable Private DNS if they want to keep using api.redwood-inference.com — otherwise they'll talk to the vpce hostname. Route tables: no route changes required beyond allowing endpoint traffic, but SGs must allow outbound 443 to our NLB's SG. For VPC peering: add route to our VPC CIDR in their RTs, ensure no CIDR overlap.

Raj (Solutions): Example AWS CLI to create an interface endpoint from their side:
```
aws ec2 create-vpc-endpoint \
  --vpc-id vpc-0123456789abcdef0 \
  --service-name com.amazonaws.vpce.us-east-1.vpce-svc-0abcdef1234567890 \
  --vpc-endpoint-type Interface \
  --subnet-ids subnet-aaa subnet-bbb subnet-ccc \
  --security-group-ids sg-0abcde12345
```
(we'll supply the `service-name`/VPCE service for them; they only need to create the endpoint and share the ENI IDs if we need to troubleshoot)

Sarah (NetEng): Operational checklist for them to send to infra team:
- Reserve a /24 per AZ for endpoint ENIs (min 3 subnets for 3 AZs)
- Create Interface VPCEs for our service (we'll give the service name)
- If using Private DNS, enable it and confirm hostname resolves to VPCE IPs
- Update SGs to allow outbound 443 to our NLB and inbound from NLB if they run callbacks
- If peering: add explicit route in each RT for our provider VPC CIDR, confirm no CIDR overlap

Emma (Security): POC security requirements:
- Generate a scoped API key with expiration (use separate key for each environment/customer)
- Restrict key by allowed hostnames/IP ranges where possible
- Enable request-level audit logs to S3 (we can provide bucket policy guidance)
- KMS: either they provide a key or we use our managed key for POC logs. Confirm which they prefer.
- If customer asks for mTLS later, that will require additional cert provisioning and likely a dedicated NLB config — not needed for this POC per their note.

Maya (Sales): They confirmed no mTLS for POC. A couple of pricing/ops q's from them: 1) How long to spin up a Dedicated pool? 2) Do you charge an onboarding fee for PrivateLink? Also they asked about Hosted vs Dedicated cost expectations for initial trial.

Raj (Solutions): Short pricing blurb to share: Hosted API — PAYG (per-token/embedding) and fastest to start; we can give trial credits for the POC. Dedicated — reserved GPUs, monthly commit, typical lead time 2–4 weeks depending on capacity (we can run a short dedicated POC if they commit to a minimal monthly). PrivateLink setup has a small one-time onboarding coordination effort (network testing + service publishing); for strategic POCs we can waive the nominal onboarding coordination fee — will confirm with sales-ops.

Maya (Sales): I'll draft a 1-page handoff for Acme infra with the checklist + the pricing note. Can you Raj/Sarah/Emma review and approve? I want to send it this afternoon.

provisioning-bot: New ticket created: INF-4821 — "acme-poc-interface-endpoint-setup" assigned to NetEng, ETA 48h.

Sarah (NetEng): Ack. I'll attach a Terraform snippet and subnet sizing guidance to INF-4821 and add a short troubleshooting checklist (DNS, ENI exhaustion, SG misconfig).

Maya (Sales): Awesome — thanks all :thumbsup: I’ll ping Acme with the doc and link to INF-4821.
